0.long_answer: Rituximab is the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody in question. Approved initially in 1997 for the treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rituximab targets the CD20 antigen on B lymphocytes. Its mechanism of action involves depletion of B-cells, thereby reducing the production of harmful autoantibodies, such as anti-ADAMTS13 antibodies in thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). When standard treatments like plasma exchange and corticosteroids are insufficient, rituximab can be added to help achieve remission in patients with TTP.
